account: On 10 August 2023 a 58-year-old man, Mr. Hải, reached Tam Anh General Hospital at 14:00. More than 24 hours after a hemorrhagic stroke, he was drowsy and weak. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a clot up to 4 cm pressing on motor and language areas. The surgeons said that without urgent surgery he faced hemiplegia, speech loss, blurred vision or death. Surgery began at 17:00 under local anesthesia. First the Modus V Synaptive robot's software fused MRI, diffusion tensor imaging, computed tomography (CT) and digital subtraction angiography scans into one 3D view of fiber tracts and clot. In that view neurosurgeon Chu Tấn Sĩ rehearsed the approach. During the operation the robot gave green, amber and red warnings when the instrument strayed from the planned path. The awake patient talked and moved on request, and he sang with the surgeon. The hospital's account states that the surgeon drew out the clot through a BrainPath port placed along the path that he had planned on the robot's software. About 40 ml of clot came out in just over 30 minutes. CT later showed none left. His movement, vision and cognition were normal, and he went home on day six. In a 2025 Cochrane review of 24 trials, Wilting and colleagues report low-certainty evidence that surgery to remove the clot may improve function and survival compared with medical care alone. They do not address robotic guidance.

ai_role.statement: The sources attribute three things to the robot's AI. It fused MRI, DTI, CT and DSA into one 3D image showing fiber tracts and clot. It allowed a rehearsal so the skull opening and path avoided the tracts. It gave green-amber-red warnings during surgery when the instrument strayed from the planned path. The surgeon placed a BrainPath port, a separate access device, along that path and drew out about 40 ml of clot. Clot removal, hemostasis and the awake function tests were done by the surgical and anesthesia teams. No source compares this with conventional surgery for this patient. None says what in the system is machine learning and what is image processing, so the counterfactual is unproven.

fields.account: On 10 August 2023 a 58-year-old man, Mr. Hải, reached Tam Anh General Hospital at 14:00. More than 24 hours after a hemorrhagic stroke, he was drowsy and weak. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a clot up to 4 cm pressing on motor and language areas. The surgeons said that without urgent surgery he faced hemiplegia, speech loss, blurred vision or death. Surgery began at 17:00 under local anesthesia. First the Modus V Synaptive robot's software fused MRI, diffusion tensor imaging, computed tomography (CT) and digital subtraction angiography scans into one 3D view of fiber tracts and clot. In that view neurosurgeon Chu Tấn Sĩ rehearsed the approach. During the operation the robot gave green, amber and red warnings when the instrument strayed from the planned path. The awake patient talked and moved on request, and he sang with the surgeon. The hospital's account states that the surgeon drew out the clot through a BrainPath port placed along the path that he had planned on the robot's software. About 40 ml of clot came out in just over 30 minutes. CT later showed none left. His movement, vision and cognition were normal, and he went home on day six. In a 2025 Cochrane review of 24 trials, Wilting and colleagues report low-certainty evidence that surgery to remove the clot may improve function and survival compared with medical care alone. They do not address robotic guidance.
